newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says five Iraq-based rebels killed in clashes.
newsitem.headline: Iran says five Iraq-based rebels killed in clashes.

text.p: Iranian tribesmen and government forces killed five members of an Iraq-based opposition group in clashes in western Iran, the Iranian news agency IRNA said on Monday.

It quoted a local official in Iran's oil-rich Khuzestan province as saying security forces killed two members of the Mujahideen Khalq armed opposition group and arrested a third after they crossed into Iran from a southern Iraqi border point on Sunday.

An official in Iran's western city of Kermanshah said on Sunday that tribesmen killed three Mujahideen members, two men and a woman, as they were trying to escape into Iraq, the agency said. The reports were monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC).
The official in Khuzestan said the incursion had been coordinated by an Iraqi intelligence officer, IRNA added.
The Mujahideen said on Monday their forces had clashed with government troops in several points along the Iran-Iraq borders but denied that any of them had been killed or arrested.

In a fax sent to Reuters from their Paris office, the group said the operations were carried out by Mujahideen members based inside Iran in an escalation of their activities. It did not give details of their operations.
Iran said on Friday the Mujahideen killed an Iranian tribesman in a cross-border attack in western Iran on Wednesday.

Tehran has blamed the group, which has several camps in Iraq near the Iranian border, for cross-border attacks and bombings in the past few years. The Mujahideen have denied attacking civilians, but have taken responsibility for striking military and economic targets.
